title: Reduce cardinality for incident_type metric label (allowlist + sampling + unknown buckets)
author: Sergio Costa
description: Context: PR #1459 introduced incident taxonomy dashboards and alert rules. During rollout review, Observability flagged that naively labeling high-volume request/edge metrics with incident_type can explode series cardinality (especially when incident-bot classification is missing/late, or when teams attempt to encode subtypes/notes). This follow-up tightens the metric labeling contract and adjusts recording rules to keep the dashboards useful without putting Prometheus/Mimir under stress. What changed: 1) Added an explicit allowlist for incident_type values used in metrics (top-level types only, no freeform). 2) Introduced two stable buckets for missing/invalid classification: incident_type="unknown" (not set) and incident_type="unclassified" (set but not in allowlist / failed validation). 3) Moved incident_type labeling off the highest-cardinality per-route/per-model series and onto lower-cardinality rollups used by the dashboards (recording rules). 4) Added a conservative sampling strategy for the remaining labeled raw series (only for error events and only for a limited set of metrics), with clear comments and defaults. 5) Updated dashboard queries and alert annotations to treat unknown/unclassified explicitly and to keep them visible (we want to drive down unknowns, not hide them). Guidance / policy baked into this repo: - Metrics must only use the top-level incident_type enum (no subtype) and must not include user/customer identifiers. - If classification is missing at emission time, emit incident_type="unknown". If a value is present but not in allowlist, normalize to incident_type="unclassified" and emit a counter for visibility. - Dashboards should break out unknown/unclassified as first-class categories so SRE can track adoption and decision-tree gaps. Rollout notes: This should be safe to deploy independently of incident-bot changes. It assumes the incident_type field exists in log/metric enrichment but tolerates it being absent. After merge, please re-run the cardinality check job in staging and confirm series counts stay within the thresholds in docs/metrics/cardinality.md. Related: ENG-4826 (metric label guardrails), ENG-4828 (dashboard build), and the earlier dashboard PR #1459.
commits: rules: shift incident taxonomy panels to recording-rule rollups
alerts: annotate unknown/unclassified and adjust grouping keys
docs: document cardinality contract and sampling defaults
ci: add cardinality check budget for incident taxonomy rules
illustrative_snippet: normalize_incident_type(value): if value == null || value == "" then "unknown" else if std.member(value, incident_type_allowlist) then value else "unclassified"; // NOTE: do not use subtype or freeform tags in metrics.
review_conversation: Allison Grant (review): We need a hard contract that incident_type is top-level only. Subtype belongs in incident tooling/events, not metrics. Please add doc language and enforce normalization to unknown/unclassified. Also please confirm dashboards still show unknown explicitly so we can track compliance.

Sergio Costa (author): Added docs/metrics/incident-type-labeling.md with the contract + examples; updated normalization to bucket missing as unknown and invalid as unclassified; updated dashboards to render unknown/unclassified as separate series and added an 'Unknown rate' stat panel.
Aisha Bello (review): Recording rules look good, but the alert grouping key still includes route in one place, which defeats the point. Can we group by tier + incident_type + owner only?
Sergio Costa (author): Good catch. Removed route/model from grouping; kept them in annotations via topk query so the page is still actionable without exploding series.
Rafael Mendes (review): Please add a metric/counter for 'normalized_to_unclassified' so we can chase down emitters. Also add a note on how incident-bot should behave if it can’t determine a type.

Sergio Costa (author): Added redwood_observability_incident_type_normalization_total{reason="unclassified"|"unknown"} and a short guidance section: emit unknown when unset; do not invent new values; add to allowlist via PR if needed.
Mei Lin (review): Can we add a simple before/after estimate for series count impact? Helpful for the program update.

Sergio Costa (author): Added numbers from staging replay in docs/metrics/cardinality.md: incident taxonomy dashboards now rely on 18 rollup series per tier vs ~400+ in the raw per-route view. Included the command to reproduce.
release_notes: Internal-only: Tightened incident_type metric labeling to prevent cardinality blowups; dashboards/alerts now treat unknown/unclassified explicitly and rely on lower-cardinality rollups.
